svg.text: Band-edge filter shape: slope honesty versus guardband cost
Same bounded waveform setup as the slope note, but now asking what the wider half-sine design pays in adjacent pickup.
The next band-edge question was the cost of the wider half-sine design

text.tspan: The previous note closed the slope loophole: the GNU Radio / fred harris half-sine construction gets much closer to the normalized near-lock target than the old proxy. This pass checks the price of that fix by
measuring how much adjacent-channel energy the band-edge filters keep capturing and how much center spacing is needed before that pickup falls below 5%.

svg.text: α = 0.20, 63 taps: sharper slope is much less selective

text.tspan: Proxy slope 0.480 needs 0.75 R_s for ≤5% pickup. Half-sine slope 0.943
needs 1.20 R_s.

svg.text: α = 0.35, 63 taps: the tradeoff stays real

text.tspan: At 1.0 R_s spacing, proxy pickup is 10.7%. Half-sine pickup is 31.5%. The
slope fix is real, and so is the spill cost.

svg.text: Tap count mostly moves slope, not spacing threshold

text.tspan: At α = 0.35 the proxy rises from slope 0.670 to 0.983, but the ≤5% spacing
stays 1.15 → 1.15 R_s. Half-sine stays 1.35 → 1.35 R_s too.
Each series shows how much energy the lower + upper band-edge filters capture from one adjacent QPSK
channel whose center is 1.0 symbol rates away. Higher means worse selectivity.

svg.text: α = 0.35, 63 taps half-sine: 31.5% pickup at 1.0 R_s

text.tspan: This is the smallest tested center spacing where the same adjacent channel drops under 5% captured
energy. Lower is cheaper on guardband. In this bounded study the design family moves this threshold
more than tap count does.

svg.text: α = 0.35, 63 taps half-sine: 1.35 R_s for ≤5% pickup
What this changes in the repo

text.tspan: The repo can now stop treating the half-sine upgrade as a free correction. It is a real implementation fix for moderate-roll-off slope, but it also keeps listening farther into a nearby channel. In this bounded setup at α =
0.35 and 63 taps, the half-sine design lifts the slope from 0.670 to 0.986, while the adjacent pickup at 1.0 R_s rises by about 2.9× and the ≤5% spacing widens from 1.15 R_s to 1.35 R_s.
• The slope note still stands: the old proxy was understating
moderate-roll-off near-lock gain.
• Small roll-off still stays weak even after the design improves.
• Half-sine is a slope-versus-selectivity tradeoff, not a free cleanup pass.
• In this bounded study, guardband cost is set more by design family than by
tap count.
• If this branch gets one more turn, measure the same tradeoff in
closed-loop behavior or with an explicit adjacent interferer level.
• Otherwise this is enough to stop pretending the better slope came for
free.
